V: V is misunderstood and intense, possibly obsessive, and usually lovely. People are sucked-in by the ease and quickness of her name when they think that she is a relaxed persona for this is rarely the truth.
Val: The name of any vehicle that has crossed the top of Australia, the middle of the USA or the entirety of Eurasia and is now covered in a 3 millimetre layer of red dust. The trip was hard and long but, by God, it was fun. She was never not going to make it, either.
Valda: Valda excels when the chips are down. She will forge on irrespective and thank Christ she does! She works hard for her family and her community, and she can cook up a storm, but like many, many other women in the Kingdom, Valda needs a lot more down time than she’s currently enjoying.
Valentina: The Queen of Glowsticks and Chewing Gum. And here at 5am, having danced non-stop for six hours or so, you’ve never seen anyone look more awake. You go girl!
Valeria: Yeah, yeah, so once upon a time she might have been something of a stress-head. Do you know, I think she's actually beginning to relax. We watched her play last week and from up in the commentary box the pre-season seems to have done her proud because the Valeria we watched play that day was a gorgeous and sensitive woman. Quite funny, as a matter of fact.
Valerie: Valerie is on her last life and she is doing okay. She used to be a worry-wart but, do you know, she learned the effectiveness of a glass of white wine at lunch time. She doesn’t worry any more.
Vanda: Vanda is the name of the sporting referee who is more famous than some of the players she presides over. She loves the spotlight and though a fair-minded and excellent umpire, she is very aware of the theatre of which she is a part. Deep down she knows the game won't alter the shape of human civilisation, but you wouldn't pick it by the look on her face. Life and Death: this is what it appears like, but it's just all part of the show.
Vaneesha: Man, she gets pissed off if you misspell her name so watch that, eh? (Vaneesha, how come? ....although, having asked that, it's not just you who is overly annoyed by this.) Anyway, Vaneesha has high standards and an ego. Let's hope she employs her intelligence in the direction of helping others and not in the acquirement of shoes. Irrespective, she hosts a kick-arse dinner party.
Vanesa: The brand new running machine lasted five goes before being shuffled out to the garage. The Ab-buster got about a dozen work outs before it, too, was pushed under the bed for good, and now the sparkling white bike machine, replete with all its computer read-outs and lights, is in the throes of it's third session. You can hear Vanesa working hard, just around the corner, there. Come on girl!.....make it HURT!! There's a lesson here: you've still got to do the work no matter where you are V!
Vanessa: The quintessential corporate woman, maybe. She's certainly organised and her hair is never curly and rarely blonde.
Vanita: You know how some actors and comediens are over-sensitive, ego-filled twats? Well not Vanita. On stage she's 'out there' but off it and certainly in her private life she's quite chilled and down to earth, and even just a little shy. Weird huh?
Vanya: The centre-piece of any large dinner party.
Vao: Vao wears an islander skirt, has a big toothy grin and she waggles her hips because she loves to dance.
Varni: Varni is no scatterbrain. She's savvy and suave and replete with girly fun if the moment takes her, and it's all part of some greater life path that both prospers and assists. Nice work, eh?
Vashti: Vashti can crack any safe anywhere. (Including any and all broken hearts.)
Vegas: Hi baby. She's spectacular. Pure and simple.
Velika: You know those dreams where you're naked but actually okay with it? Well that's like a Velika Dream, except here you're in something of a maze, you're lost and, yes, you're naked. Either way, you walk around with a smile on your face in the knowledge that fun and ludicrous scenarios are just around the corner. Bravo!
Velona: As a brave she-warrior in a past life, Velona gets bored at the drop of a hat in this one. How does she handle it? Easy. She drinks and she makes grand sweeping statements with her arms out. She's great fun to watch, especially as she's knocked over more glasses and carafes than anyone. God love her!
Velvet: Mmmm, intersting. Some trampolines are just too bouncy, aren't they? Now, Velvet, were you spoilt as a little girl? You weren't? Okay, great then. That explains why you've matured early, have a massive circle of friends and why you tend to do things you say you're going to do. That's right, isn't it?...Velvet?...
Venetta: Donald Trump, eat your heart out. Except this woman has better hair and she's far sexier. The tougher the opposition the better she plays.
Venus:
Venus is the only woman on Earth to have a running account at three different exclusive rug and carpet shops at the same time. There is some debate at two of the shops, arrived at independently of each other, mind you, that she buys all of these new rugs just so she can rip all her gear off and lounge around all over them like a glorious naked cheetah cub after a big feed. Is anyone taking photos of her while she's doing this?
They should.
Vera:
Option A:  So long as she’s comfortable in her clothes Vera doesn’t care what she looks like. She loves all cheeses, detests all children and in a past life she was a sturdy curtain rail.

Option B: Tree lopper.
Verity:
Option A: Verity has an intricate and geometrically perfect haircut, her spectacles match her handbag and she has a beautiful speaking voice.

Option B: Tartare sauce: To be served with cold fish, shellfish and cold vegetables. Keep in the refrigerator until needed.
Verlie:
Verlie is the kind of woman who loves the idea of visiting the Louvre, until she walks through the entrance. Her reaction to the whole day can be summed up by her reaction to the Mona Lisa.
“Oh you’ve got to be kidding. That's it?” she blurts, finally fed up. “Okay, fuck this, let’s go and get a drink.”
Verna: The Gnu. She’s persistent, she’s unorthodox with the arena of romance and, sure, she's abit ungainly, especially when she runs, but you just try getting anywhere near her supper.
Verne: Verne is so lovely and curt and cute and herself that she could probably start her own religion. Verne, we love you up here in the box so please, just keep doing you’re job. Cheers. Management.
Vernetta:
The young boys blast into the kitchen where Vernetta is sitting on a stool, reading the Financial Review and sipping on a nice glass of unwooded chardonnay. Her bracelets clink on the spotless marble bench top as she places the glass back down. 
“All right, if you’re going to stay here quieten down otherwise go out and talk on the verandah,” she says, bothered. “This is the first moment I’ve had to myself all day.”
“Okay, mum,” her son says. “Come on fellas, let’s go outside.”
Secretly, all her son's friends lust after her but that’s another story.
Verona:
"On a cold and grey Chicago morn'
and a poor little baby child is born,
in the ghetto….."

Yes, Elvis sung it well, and Verona is the sort of woman who, in such a situation, would fight, and think, and bust her way through such adversity. She's kind, she's artistic, and you just watch her put the gloves on if need be.
Veronica: Veronica wears a layered petticoat under her skirt and the spectacles on her face aren’t dissimilar in style to those worn by Dame Edna Everage.
Veronika: For all her airs and graces, Veronika has the embarrassing knack of coming out of the girls' bathroom with toilet paper stuck to her foot.
Vettie: Vettie Biscetti. She’s got heaps of scrapes and scars on her legs and knees because she runs full tilt into the guns, all the time, dragging whoever she can, kicking and screaming with her (even though they secretly love it, and need to be dragged).
Vianna: Long-limbed and complex, Vianna looks as though she's just walked straight out of a French fashion shoot. Many find her unapproachable, and heavens-be-to-mercy, is she just about fed up with that idea or what? Go and say hello, for god's sake. If anything she's just doing what many of us do, and that is to hope that no one exposes her for not really being sure of what she's doing, or why, at any given time.
Vic: The super-chilled out Victoria. The ego and all the hype is still there, which is a good thing, but she won’t kick you under the dinner table if you mention to the assembled group of how out-of-it she got the other night, and what she did afterwards.
Vick: This girl is as comfortable with herself and the world as anyone and 95% of the time, at least, she cruises along with a quietly determined air, as if life is all too easy. Yet, why does it feel like something is still missing?....
Vickey: In a past life Vickey was a Scottish warrior who fought the English on the moors and valleys of the North. Her battle cry was always the loudest, too. And here in the modern world not much as changed, God bless her. She eats confrontation for breakfast.
Vicki: Highly intelligent and picky, ‘V’ hates the fact that every second person spells her name wrong.
Vickie: Hello Vickie, now don't worry. But, yes, you too are highly intelligent and picky, and does it really matter that every second person misspells your name? Trust me, if you and those around you have your health, then does anything else really matter?
Vicky: Yes, I know, but Vicky too is highly intelligent and picky, and she also hates it that every second person spells her name wrong. (Blah blah blah…..go and complain to someone else!)
Victoria: Victoria is the name of a big, beautiful mare. Her chestnut coat has a glorious lustre and she stands before you proud, glistening and powerful. However, how close you get to her will be up to her, and her alone. She may deem you worthy of little more than a kick in the face; then again she may let you run your hands through her glorious mane with only love on her mind. Good luck!
Vicy:
(Pronounced Vicky). Question: Which idiotic parent decided this should be the spelling, Vicy? Anyway, all ‘Vickys’, irrespective of spelling, are hard-fighting, ambitious, highly intelligent and uncompromising, and this Vicy is no different. However, a wee caviat - if YOU, Vicy, decided to spell your name this way purely as a means to be different you need to find yourself a  hobby real quick, and especially if you get on your high horse about it, which, sadly, is a common theme among all your Vicki/Vicky/Vikki etc sisters. 
The End.
Vida: The effusive control freak – which means that there’s a good chance she’s South African. She drinks a ton of coffee.
Vien: V is for Victory! Yet Vien is also understated and sensual, and she loves it when all her guests leave (whom she adores) so she can just flop into her favourite lounge chair and take a moment to chill-the-fuck-out.
Vieve: Like the captain of an aircraft with one of its four engines behaving badly, Vieve is constantly looking for somewhere to land just in case. Is she a worrier? Well, not particularly, but you need to be on the lookout for catastrophe, that's all. In reality, and despite the furrowed brow, life for Vieve usually sails along quite nicely.
Viki:
Yeah yeah Viki, we know about your spelling woes. And though you’ll hate the spelling of the name of the woman we’re sending you to, her rather lovely description fits you very well. Please go and read Vickey. Although you do attend fine-dining restaurants more often, and whence there you know which cutlery to use for each course.
Love, Management.
Vikki: Ever seen a spider weave its web from close up? They're amazing creatures. All those flailing arms and elbows, yet they manage to be highly organised. Indeed, this is Vikki to a ‘T'. Like the rest of the species (Vicky, Vicki, Vickie etc etc) Vikki hates it when you get her name wrong, but that's okay. She gets so much done in her spare time that we can forgive her occasional psychotic outburst. Not one to mess with.
Vilma: Vilma's seriousness has gone into remission, thank God! But don't give her a map of any kind. It'll stress her out to the max, immediately.
Vina: Well, Vina does like a vino, but she’s serious and responsible when she needs to be, probably more than she needs to be, truth be told. Vina seems to be one of those people who launches into things - i.e. a new job, into the car or simply into the bathroom to have a shower - having forgotten most of what she wanted to bring with her. It’s bloody frustrating, both for her and for those who are waiting.
Viola: We all have a niche to fill, of course, but like the male Bryson, Viola could do with a few more moments of pure, unadulterated, ill-thought out impulsiveness. Is she a drama queen?….mmmm…not always.
Violaine: Protective of her assets (property, investments, savings, etc). Sex doesn't really come into it.
Violet: The angel that watches over all of us. She’s thousands of years old, has a deity-like wisdom, and can’t understand why everyone seems so stressed, angry and depressed these days.
Virginia: Virginia is a chilled-out lady who, at 60 years of age, still looks amazing in a ball gown or a bikini. She has tons of friends (like Denise, Jackie and Pam) and when they get together at the cafe every Thursday morning, without fail, they talk so much that no one nearby is able to hear themselves think.
Viv: There aren’t many words that can be said in the course of normal relaxed breathing – Viv is one of them. Her name, therefore, rhymes with Yes, Sure, Anytime, Not a problem, If you like, If I like, Whatever you want, Whatever she wants and Whatever you feel like. And what does that all mean? That Viv is cool and interested, and possibly pretty sexy.
Vivian:
“Viv - i - an”…..rhymes with….. “On - her - own.” 
She lives in the city and spent a long time getting over a heroin habit that has enabled her, at least, to experience the spiritual world in ways that she never knew possible. Now that she’s clean, she runs her own business that sells crystals and aromatic oils. There’s a psychic out the back on Tuesdays.
Vivien:
Misadventure is often Vivien’s middle name – not so much that she’ll end up in jail, but certainly enough to get caught shagging in a carpark somewhere, and yes, usually when she’s a younger lass. In adulthood Vivien is educated and travelled, or at least she gives that impression, and she’ll happily deal with the label of ‘arrogant’ if it means she gets to a good time faster. She’s never as demure as you think.
Is all that complicated enough for you?
Good.
Welcome to Vivien.
Vivienne: Every time Vivienne hears that song about driving a sports car through Paris she weeps that she never got the chance. (Note to Vivienne: Honey, fuck it, steal some money if you have to and go do it! What's the worst thing that will happen? Have you watched the news lately? Love Management. x)
Vivina: She will probably insist that her name be pronounced 'Vee-Vine-Arr', in which case give her the keys, tell her there's plenty of booze in the fridge and then take-off for the weekend. She'll be alright. She'll spend most of her time on the phone, anyway.
Voula: Sensual and determined, as a businesswoman with a Greek heritage Voula loves it when her work life, her family life and the general bullshit we all have to deal with form a collective bed of screaming, hilarious chaos.
